s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ataxia with spasms and myoclonus
salient_findings: Hypometric saccades and truncal and limb ataxia
Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz
key_facts: Male patient in his 70s
20-year history of progressive ataxia
8-month history of throat spasms
Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Throat spasms did not affect ability to speak or eat
Hypometric saccades present
Truncal and limb ataxia present
Decreased vibratory sense with inability to ambulate
Bradykinesia and mild rigidity present
Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz
Patient unable to stop myoclonus of the palate with voluntary use of palatal musculature
No clicking noted by patient or examiners
Genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 was normal
MRI brain without contrast showed severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

shortlist.label: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 7
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

shortlist.label: Multiple system atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia, bradykinesia, and mild rigidity

shortlist.label: Palatal myoclonus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz

shortlist.label: Dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia, myoclonus, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

raw.rationale: The patient's progressive ataxia, bradykinesia, mild rigidity, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with multiple system atrophy. The presence of palatal myoclonus also supports this diagnosis, as it can be a feature of multiple system atrophy.

rejected.label: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 7
rejected.why: Genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 was normal, and while type 7 was not explicitly tested, the presence of other symptoms such as bradykinesia and mild rigidity suggests a more complex disorder like multiple system atrophy

rejected.label: Palatal myoclonus syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has palatal myoclonus, this condition alone does not explain the full range of symptoms, including progressive ataxia, bradykinesia, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

rejected.label: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 8
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and normal genetic testing for other spinocerebellar ataxia types, along with the presence of extracerebellar symptoms like bradykinesia and mild rigidity, make multiple system atrophy a more comprehensive diagnosis

rejected.label: Dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a combination of ataxia, myoclonus, and dementia, but the patient's specific constellation of symptoms and the absence of noted dementia or specific mention of other characteristic features make multiple system atrophy a more fitting diagnosis
